title: CloudFront: edge locations, origins and invalidation

videos.script: A customer in Manaus opens the shop's page. Every image on it travels from São Paulo, thousands of kilometres, every time. {{far}} CloudFront puts a copy of those images near the customer instead. {{edges}} AWS runs hundreds of edge locations around the world. The first request for an image goes all the way back to the shop. Every request after it is answered from the edge. {{origins}} You will build a distribution in moto with two origins. The shop's bucket, which only CloudFront may read. And the load balancer from lesson 22, for the pages. {{behaviours}} A path decides which origin answers, and how long the edge may keep what it got. {{invalidate}} Then the moment every team meets: a file changed, and the edges still have the old one. You can tell them to forget it, which is called an invalidation. Or you can give the new file a new name, which is better, and the lesson says why. {{price}} Last, the price list. Sending a gigabyte to the internet through CloudFront costs less than sending it straight from São Paulo, and the lesson reads both lines. {{end}}
